Overview

Build the future of AI. From anywhere in the world.

Geek Room presents a global, fully virtual AI-focused hackathon, open to developers, students, researchers, and builders from any country, background, and skill level.

Bring your ideas, experiment with cutting-edge AI technologies, solve real-world challenges, and build alongside a global community of innovators, all from wherever you are.

With multiple tracks, technologies, and challenges, participants can choose what they want to build and how they want to build it.

WHY PARTICIPATE?
Global and open to everyone across countries, backgrounds, and skill levels.
AI-focused challenges across multiple tracks and technologies.
Build using technologies from leading industry partners.
100% virtual, allowing you to participate from anywhere.
Compete for prizes, recognition, and opportunities.
Connect and collaborate with builders from around the world.
Showcase your project to leading companies and the wider developer community.

One idea. One team. One global stage.

Organized by Geek Room with ❤️

Themes
Build a Coding Agent That Gets the Job Done on the Fewest Tokens

Build an AI coding agent that completes real development tasks while minimizing token consumption and operational costs. The agent must continue working through provider outages, enforce individual spending limits, protect confidential repositories by using local models, and require user approval before performing risky operations such as file writes, shell commands, or Git actions. The solution should demonstrate efficient and reliable coding workflows without compromising correctness, privacy, or security.

AI Agents & Intelligent Systems
Read more
Build a Benchmarking Platform for AI Agents, Not Just Models

Build a framework-independent benchmarking platform that evaluates AI agents against identical tasks. The platform must measure task success, execution steps, tool calls, token usage, cost, and completion time across repeated runs. It should also test how agents respond to failing tools, unavailable models, and misleading instructions, while providing a comparison interface with detailed execution traces to help developers understand agent performance and reliability.

AI Agents & Intelligent Systems
Read more
Build an Agent That Pentests a Target on Its Own

Build an autonomous AI agent capable of performing authorized penetration testing inside a strictly isolated laboratory environment. The agent must explore permitted targets using real security tools, interpret results, independently decide its next actions, and work toward predefined security objectives. The solution must strictly respect the provided scope, recover from unsuccessful attempts, and generate actionable security reports containing findings, evidence, severity, and remediation recommendations.

AI Agents & Intelligent Systems
Read more
Open-Source Bifrost Gateway

Extend the open-source Bifrost gateway with a practical feature that solves a real problem for developers or gateway operators. This could include a plugin, provider integration, caching or routing capability, user interface, or developer tool. The solution must use supported extension points, work with a standard Bifrost installation, and include clear setup instructions, documentation, and tests. The final contribution should be suitable for consideration as an upstream open-source pull request.

AI Agents & Intelligent Systems
Read more
Tavily Research Agent

Build an AI-powered research agent that prepares a concise, one-page briefing before a meeting. Given a company or person and a scheduled meeting time, the agent should research relevant developments from the preceding 30 days, including news, launches, hires, and other important updates. The briefing should provide source-backed findings, useful discussion points, and open questions to help users prepare for meaningful conversations.

AI Agents & Intelligent Systems
Read more
Build a Stale-Answer Detector for AI Applications

Build an AI-powered verification system that identifies outdated information in LLM-generated answers. The system should detect potentially stale claims involving pricing, API versions, regulations, or company information, re-verify them against live web sources, and provide a freshness score for each claim. The solution should help users distinguish current, reliable information from potentially outdated AI-generated responses using both Tavily and Bifrost.

AI Agents & Intelligent Systems

READ THIS IN FULL Problem statements go live on 1 Nov, and the prototype submission window opens at the same time. Choose your challenge, build your AI-powered solution, and submit your working prototype within the two-week building window. Project Submission Instructions

Select your primary problem statement from the Theme dropdown.

You can build a project using Bifrost by Maxim AI, Tavily, or both technologies together. However, you are also allowed to submit 2 separate projects on the 2 technologies.

If you're building a merged project that addresses a Bifrost challenge along with a Tavily challenge, select the Bifrost challenge as your primary problem statement and use the optional Tavily integration checkbox to indicate the additional challenge.

If you're building only a Tavily project, simply select the relevant Tavily problem statement as your primary theme. And if you're submitting for both the technologies, make sure that you go ahead and submit the provided submission form in full, providing the details for both the projects.

Your GitHub repository must be public and include a detailed README covering your project, installation steps, implementation, and technologies used.

Your pitch deck should explain the problem, your solution, technical architecture, and working prototype. If you've combined both technologies, clearly demonstrate how each contributes to your project.

A deployed application is not mandatory, but you're welcome to share a live demo or demonstration video.

Rules
1. Build During the Hackathon

Projects should be substantially developed during the official hackathon period. Existing libraries, frameworks, boilerplate, and supporting infrastructure may be used, but the core project should be created during the hackathon.

2. AI Usage

Participants are encouraged to use AI models, agents, APIs, vector databases, frameworks, and other AI technologies. The use of AI tools should be clearly mentioned in the project submission where applicable.

3. Discord & Official Communication

All participants are required to join the official hackathon Discord server. Discord will be used for team communication, important announcements, challenge updates, workshops, technical guidance, and hackathon-related support.

Participants are responsible for checking the official Discord channels regularly so they do not miss important updates, deadlines, or announcements.

Participants are responsible for checking the official Discord channels regularly so they do not miss important updates, deadlines, or announcements.

4. Team Size

Teams can consist of 1–4 members. Each participant can be part of only one team.

5. Original Work

All submissions must be original work or use components that participants have the legal right to use. Plagiarism or unauthorized use of intellectual property will result in disqualification.

6. Third-Party Tools

Participants may use third-party APIs, SDKs, datasets, open-source software, and developer tools, provided they comply with the applicable licenses and terms of service.

7. Submission Requirements

Each submission must include:

A working project or demo
Source code or repository
Project description
Explanation of the problem being solved
Technologies and tools used
Explanation of how AI is used in the solution
Demo video, if required

Build Resources:
Participants can explore the Bifrost GitHub repository as a technical resource while building their projects.

8. One Submission per Team

Each team may submit only one final project.

9. Responsible Development

Projects must comply with applicable laws and platform policies. Projects involving illegal activities, malicious software, fraud, harassment, or harmful content may be disqualified.

10. Judging Criteria

Projects will be evaluated based on:

Innovation
Technical execution
Problem and potential impact
Use of AI
User experience
Scalability and potential
11. Organizer’s Decision

The organizers reserve the right to disqualify submissions that violate the rules, eligibility requirements, or spirit of the hackathon.
